My travels / San Miguel de Allende / Dolores Hidalgo

Mexico · from San Miguel de Allende

An afternoon in
Dolores Hidalgo

Independence history, ranchera music, a proper Mexican lunch and a scoop of something unexpected.

Depart at 12:00 pm · Return around 7:30–8:00 pm.

Smaller and less touristy than San Miguel, Dolores Hidalgo has an extraordinary place in Mexican history: this is where the movement for Mexican independence began in 1810. Our half-day plan brings together the historic centre, two fascinating museums, famous unusual ice creams and colourful ceramics.

Before you go

Opening hours

  • Carnitas Vicente 3: 9 am–5 pm.
  • Casa de Hidalgo: 10 am–4 pm, Wednesday–Sunday; closed Monday and Tuesday.
  • José Alfredo Jiménez museum: 11 am–5:30 pm.
  • Cerámica Almita: closes at 7 pm.
  • Helados Josué and Parroquia: no hours listed on Google Maps.

Hours checked on Google Maps on 23 October 2026. They can change; check again before visiting.

On foot in the historic centre

Your walking route

  1. Museo Casa de Hidalgo
  2. Lunch at Carnitas Vicente 3
  3. Casa Museo José Alfredo Jiménez
  4. Parroquia & Jardín Principal
  5. Try the famous nieves
  6. Corredor Artesanal José Alfredo Jiménez

Start at Casa de Hidalgo, then walk between the six stops in the historic centre.

Leave room to wander

Our priorities

Casa de Hidalgo, the church and plaza, the José Alfredo Jiménez museum, and the ice creams. Everything else is a bonus: a lovely mix of Mexican history, everyday town life and local culture.

Support local women

If you can afford to and would like to, consider donating to Red Nacional de Refugios to support women and children experiencing domestic violence.

I don’t receive any money or commission from these donations. Supporting local women matters to me, and this is one small way to give back to the places I visit. It takes all of us to stand against gender-based and domestic violence.
